name: de.skysolar/sky-solar
title: Sky Solar
description: Solar installer for Munich and Rosenheim: 3D solar roof check, local subsidies, EEG feed-in, guide.

tools.name: check_service_area
tools.description: Check whether Sky Solar serves a German postcode. Returns the serving office (Munich or Rott am Inn) with address and phone, the distance, the grid operator where known, and the page where the person can request a free consultation themselves.

locale.description: Language of the answer: de (German) or en (English).

tools.name: find_subsidies
tools.description: Municipal grants for rooftop solar, home batteries and plug-in solar (Balkonkraftwerk) for a postcode anywhere in Oberbayern (Upper Bavaria, all 500 municipalities from Ingolstadt to Berchtesgaden): amounts, guideline link and date, how to apply and when work may start. With a planned system (plan) it also estimates the grant. Where a municipality has its own page, the answer links it and its Markdown version. Without guarantee.

locale.description: Language of the answer: de (German) or en (English).

roofKwp.description: Planned rooftop solar system in kWp

batteryKwh.description: Planned home battery in kWh (usable capacity)

roofCostEur.description: Cost of the rooftop system from the quote, euros (only needed where the grant is a share of the cost)

wallbox.description: A wallbox is installed at the same time

pluginStorage.description: The plug-in solar system has its own battery

reminder.description: true: attach a calendar reminder (.ics file, an embedded resource) to look again, for a municipality whose programme is closed (budget used up, suspended or ended).

reminder_date.description: The reminder's day (YYYY-MM-DD) instead of the January default.

tools.name: area_figures
tools.description: What our own solar roof check found over the family houses of a München district or of a town with a subsidy page: the typical house (modules, kWp, kWh a year), how many houses have room for a good system, the share of the household's power that comes from its own roof without and with a 5 or 10 kWh battery, the shade loss, and the area's own finding (what stands out against the rest of München). Totals and middle values over a sample of the area's houses, never a single house or address. With the link to the area's page. For a particular roof use find_house and plan_roof.

place.description: A München district (Stadtbezirk, e.g. "Pasing-Obermenzing", "Trudering", "Solln"; also its number or a neighbourhood in it) or a town with a subsidy page (e.g. "Pullach", "Garching").

locale.description: Language of the answer: de (German) or en (English).

tools.name: eeg_feed_in
tools.description: What a rooftop solar system in Germany earns for the power it feeds into the grid over 20 years: today's fixed payment for systems running by 31 Dec 2026, or the government draft EEG 2027 for later ones. Illustration with Munich yields, not a quote.

startYear.description: Year the system starts operating, any year from 2026.

selfUseShare.description: Share of the yield used at home, 0 to 1

orientation.description: Roof orientation (yield from PVGIS for Munich)

fullFeedIn.description: Feed everything into the grid (only for systems starting in 2026)

afterTransition.description: From 2027: sell through a direct marketer, or hand the power over for free

tools.name: size_system
tools.description: How big a rooftop solar system should be for a household near Munich: from today's consumption plus a planned heat pump or electric car, the roof orientation and (optionally) the usable roof area. Uses the same model as the calculator in Sky Solar's guide. An illustration, not a quote.

heatPumpKwh.description: Extra kWh a year for a planned heat pump (0 if none)

carKwh.description: Extra kWh a year for a planned electric car charged at home (0 if none)

roofM2.description: Usable roof area in m² (without windows, chimneys, shaded parts), if known

locale.description: Language of the answer: de (German) or en (English).

tools.name: battery_savings
tools.description: What a home battery saves a year and over its life, and a sensible size by the Verbraucherzentrale rule of thumb. Uses the same model as the calculator in Sky Solar's guide. An illustration, not a quote.

shiftedKwh.description: kWh a year the battery moves from midday to the evening. Default 1,500: the Verbraucherzentrale example for a home battery

tools.name: company_facts

locale.description: Language of the answer: de (German) or en (English).

tools.name: find_house
tools.description: Find a building in Bavaria by its address, for the solar roof check. Returns up to 5 matches with a house id (up to 20 when the address has no house number yet). If several match, ask the person which one before planning. If the person knows only the town (or a village of it), give just that name: the answer lists the town's streets (a village is mapped to its town only where the data knows it; in a big town the list waits for the first letters of a street), and a street with its town lists its house numbers.

address.description: Street, house number and town (or postcode) in Bavaria, e.g. "Forststraße 10, Neuried"; or only the town (or a village of it) when the person knows only the place, e.g. "Halblech", and the answer lists its streets.

tools.name: plan_roof
tools.description: Plan solar modules on a house's roof from the Bavarian 3D building model, the aerial photo and the laser scan, exactly as Sky Solar's solar roof check page does: modules, kWp, kWh a year with measured weather, shade loss and self-use with and without a battery, each roof face with tilt and direction, the obstacles found, money a year at public rates (own use and feed-in) for a choice of battery sizes (none, or 4 to 20 kWh; any whole kWh in between on request), the municipal subsidy, the price guide ("from" and "typically around", only inside Sky Solar's service area) and the payback (on the person's own offer price, else on the guide's upper value), kWh month by month and per face, the worst shade casters, questions about unsure spots for the person and what else to ask them, notes on likely model errors, and a solar roof check link that opens this plan in 3D for the person to check, change and send an enquiry from. On a new plan (house) where the aerial photo speaks against the roof's outline, the AI outline check runs by itself, as on the page: "applied" says what it changed. A link is read as it is; "notes" says when the outline may still be wrong. Give house (from find_house) for a new plan, or link to read and explain a plan the person already has. Pass the person's answers to the questions with answers. Works outside Sky Solar's service area too and says so. An example, not a quote; the only prices are the report's price guide (price_guide: "from" and "typically around", a rough guide, never an offer), and the payback counts the person's own offer or, without one, that recommendation.

house.description: The house id from find_house ("musterhaus" is the example house).

link.description: A solar roof check link (https://pv.skysolar.de/dachcheck/#d=…), as plan_roof, edit_roof or the solar roof check page gave it.

id.description: The id of a question from the last answer.

obstacle.description: true: there is an obstacle there; false: there is none.

geometry.description: true: add a complete geometry snapshot to the answer (the default stays short): for every face and dormer roof its outline, size, usable box and the eave and slope axes (with compass bearings), every module with its face, position in the face's own metres and orientation, the module fields (rows × columns), and the obstacles with their outlines and clearances.

consumption_kwh.description: The household's electricity use a year, kWh, without car or heat pump (default 4,500).

battery_kwh.description: Battery size, kWh: 0 for none, or a whole number from 4 to 20 (default 8).

battery_type.description: The battery's type, both DC-coupled hybrid systems: "nv5" (low voltage, the default) charges and discharges at most 5 kW whatever its size; "hv1c" (high voltage) at most 1C, as many kW as it has kWh (10 kWh: 10 kW, 4 kWh: only 4 kW).

ev.description: An electric car is (or will be) charged at home: by default 15,000 km a year, about 2,955 kWh, charged in the evening (edit_roof device sets km, when and how fast).

heat_pump.description: A heat pump heats the house: by default about 4,500 kWh a year, mostly in winter (edit_roof device sets the person's own figure).

offer_eur.description: The total price on an offer the person already has, euros before any subsidy (0 clears it), never a price of Sky Solar's: the payback then counts it.

roof_step.description: How demanding the roof is for the price guide: "simple" (one field, plain tiles), "normal", "complex" (several directions, many small fields, Biberschwanz tiles); "auto" (the default) works it out from the plan.

optimizers.description: The person wants module optimizers: they are in both prices of the price guide.

backup_power.description: The person wants backup power (Notstrom): it is in both prices of the price guide.

tools.name: edit_roof
tools.description: Improve a solar roof check plan from what the person knows: a building plan, photos, measurements or answers. Read the numbers yourself (tilt, overhang, sizes, where a chimney is) and pass them as edits: slope (tilt and direction of a face), overhang (move an eave or end in or out), split a face, remove or restore a face, add_face (an extension or garage against a wall), add, remove or confirm obstacles (with height_m), change_kind (e.g. a found dormer to a flat-roofed or hipped one, or a chimney to a vent), colour (sheet metal, window frames, …), covering (tiles, Falzblech, Trapezblech, rack tilt 5/10/15°, flat-roof racks; on a flat dormer roof it decides racks or flush), dormer_modules, fill_dormer and clear_dormer (one dormer's roof full of modules, or none), modules (arrangement as the page names it: „Ästhetisch“ design, „Ordentlich“ tidy, „Maximal“ most; orientation incl. mixed; module type), add_part or remove_part (an attached building part from "building_parts", e.g. the other half of a semi-detached house), remove_tree, restore_tree or tree_height (trees from "shade", the worst shade casters first), edit_obstacle (move, resize, raise, turn or give a free four-cornered outline to any obstacle, found or own), face_outline (any outline by corners, as the editor drags them), reset_face („Wie gemessen“), unsplit, add_face also with corners_m (any shape), drawn_face (eave height) and delete_face, turn_racks (flat roofs and racked dormer roofs), find_similar („Ähnliche finden“ on the aerial photo), check_outline (the AI outline check), search_again, module fields by hand (lay_by_hand, add_modules as a block of rows and columns, remove_modules, move_field, turn_field; also on dormer roofs from "dormer_roofs"; on flat roofs the modules keep standing on their racks), the modules in an area together as the page selects them (move_modules, turn_modules, set_module_type for a module type of their own; remove_modules takes an area too) and household (incl. offer_eur, the price on an offer the person has, for the payback the link shows; roof_step, optimizers and backup_power for the price guide). Own obstacle ids (u:<n>) keep their numbers for the whole call. To rebuild a layout the person drew, lay the face by hand and place its fields. Faces are named by the ids in plan_roof's "faces", which give facing, building (house or attached part), size and eave_overhang_m to tell them apart; when two could fit, ask the person. Places on a face are metres up from the eave (horizontal, as on a drawing from above) and from the face's left end seen from below, standing in front of the roof. Each applied sentence says how many modules that edit added or took away. Returns the new link and figures, one sentence per change to confirm with the person, and the edits it turned down with the reason. The old link keeps working; nothing is stored.

consumption_kwh.description: The household's electricity use a year, kWh, without car or heat pump (default 4,500).

battery_kwh.description: Battery size, kWh: 0 for none, or a whole number from 4 to 20 (default 8).

battery_type.description: The battery's type, both DC-coupled hybrid systems: "nv5" (low voltage, the default) charges and discharges at most 5 kW whatever its size; "hv1c" (high voltage) at most 1C, as many kW as it has kWh (10 kWh: 10 kW, 4 kWh: only 4 kW).

ev.description: An electric car is (or will be) charged at home: by default 15,000 km a year, about 2,955 kWh, charged in the evening (edit_roof device sets km, when and how fast).

heat_pump.description: A heat pump heats the house: by default about 4,500 kWh a year, mostly in winter (edit_roof device sets the person's own figure).

offer_eur.description: The total price on an offer the person already has, euros before any subsidy (0 clears it), never a price of Sky Solar's: the payback then counts it.

roof_step.description: How demanding the roof is for the price guide: "simple" (one field, plain tiles), "normal", "complex" (several directions, many small fields, Biberschwanz tiles); "auto" (the default) works it out from the plan.

optimizers.description: The person wants module optimizers: they are in both prices of the price guide.

backup_power.description: The person wants backup power (Notstrom): it is in both prices of the price guide.

modules.description: How many modules: the nearest step of the plan's size ladder (summary.size.steps lists them). Each step is a tidy field, never modules scattered about.

to.description: "target": the size that suits the household (a year's yield 1.5 to 2 times its use, e-car and heat pump in), and it follows the household from then on; "whole": the whole roof; "smaller", "larger": one step along the ladder, as the page's − and +.

oneOf.description: How big the system is (the page's "− 24 Module +"): give modules or to, not both.

device.description: "ev": an electric car charged at home (with its wallbox); "heat_pump": an air-to-water heat pump heating the house and its water; "heating_rod": the heat pump's electric rod (needs the heat pump; off by default); "battery": the home battery, only its colour (its size is household.battery_kwh, its type household.battery_type); "dishwasher", "washer", "dryer": a shiftable appliance run at a set time.

on.description: false takes the device out (its settings go with it); true or left out puts it in, and even with no settings records that the person answered for it (the defaults are right), so ask_the_person stops asking.

km_per_year.description: ev: km a year charged at home (default 15000); at 19.7 kWh per 100 km (ADAC Ecotest 2023 average, at the socket).

charging.description: ev: when the car is at home to charge: "evening" (default, from 18:00), "daytime" (home office or retired, from 11:00), "weekend" (Saturday and Sunday from 11:00).

charge_kw.description: ev: charging power, kW: 2.3, 3.7, 7.4, 11, 22 (default 11, a usual wallbox).

charges_per_week.description: ev: charging sessions a week, 1 to 7 (default 7, every day); each takes what built up since the last. Not for "weekend".

kwh_per_year.description: heat_pump: its electricity a year in kWh (its meter, the bill or the installer's figure), or "estimate" for ours (4,500 kWh).

kwh_per_run.description: appliance: kWh per run (defaults: dishwasher 0.85, washer 0.8, dryer 1.5; EU label and Verbraucherzentrale figures; a dryer without a heat pump about 3.4).

peak_kw.description: appliance: kW of its heating peak (defaults: dishwasher 2, washer 2, dryer 0.8).

peak_minutes.description: appliance: how long the peak lasts, minutes, all of it together (defaults: dishwasher 20, washer 15, dryer 100).

runs_per_week.description: appliance: runs a week, evenly over the week (defaults: dishwasher 5.4, washer 4.2, dryer 2).

start.description: appliance: when it starts, "HH:MM" (to ten minutes) or "sun" for the midday window, a fixed time as a delay timer sets it (dishwasher 12:00, washer 11:00, dryer 14:00).

rod_kw.description: heating_rod: its power, kW (default 6; rods have 3 to 9 kW).

bivalence_c.description: heating_rod: the outdoor temperature below which it helps, °C (default -5).

hot_water_percent.description: heating_rod: share of the hot water it heats instead of the heat pump, % (default 0), each morning. The rod's kWh stay inside the heat pump's kWh a year.

colour.description: The device's colour as the 3D view draws it by the house (changes no figure): heat_pump and battery silver, white, anthracite, black (default silver); ev (the car's paint) silver, white, anthracite, black, blue, red (default silver).

wallbox_colour.description: ev: the wallbox's colour, white, silver, anthracite, black (default white).

oneOf.description: An e-car, a heat pump, its heating rod or a shiftable appliance with its own load curve: on or off, its settings and its colour (also the battery's colour).

answers.description: The person's answers to the last answer's "questions".

id.description: The id of a question from the last answer.

obstacle.description: true: there is an obstacle there; false: there is none.

geometry.description: true: add a complete geometry snapshot to the answer (the default stays short): for every face and dormer roof its outline, size, usable box and the eave and slope axes (with compass bearings), every module with its face, position in the face's own metres and orientation, the module fields (rows × columns), and the obstacles with their outlines and clearances.

tools.name: roof_edit_help
tools.description: The full text of one or more edit_roof edits: every field with its defaults, its special cases and what the answer reports. The tool list gives only each field's first sentence; call this when that leaves a question, or after an edit was turned down. Nothing is planned or changed.

tools.name: compare_plans
tools.description: Compare 2 to 4 variants of one house's solar roof check plan side by side, as the page's „Varianten vergleichen“ does: give links (plans you already have, e.g. from edit_roof), or link and variants, each the plan with a few edit_roof edits (a battery size or none, a roof face off or on, an e-car or a heat pump, an offer price). Answers a table with, per plan: modules, kWp, kWh a year with measured weather, own use (share of the roof's power used in the house), autarky, self-used, fed-in and grid kWh, days without the grid, euros a year at public rates, kWh by month, the payback (on the person's own offer where one holds for that plan's system, else on that plan's upper price-guide value), its link, and the difference to the first plan; plus the first plan's battery curve: what each further kWh of battery adds a year, and from about which size each kWh adds little; and `day_views`: the same three real days of the person's weather (sunny, cloudy, winter) for every plan, hour by hour (solar, consumption, from the sun, to and from the battery, to and from the grid), the page's day view. Appliances and a heating rod are variants too (edit_roof device). One weather fetch for all. Nothing is stored; each variant comes back as its own link. An example, not a quote; the only prices are each plan's price guide, a guide and never an offer.

links.description: 2 to 4 solar roof check links of the same house; the first is the one the others are compared with (usually the person's plan).

items.description: A solar roof check link (https://pv.skysolar.de/dachcheck/#d=…), as plan_roof, edit_roof or the solar roof check page gave it.

link.description: One plan to compare variants of (with variants).

variants.description: 1 to 3 variants of the plan in link, each the plan with a few edits: a battery size (household battery_kwh, 0 for none) or type (household battery_type), a face off or on (remove_face, restore_face), an e-car, a heat pump or its heating rod (household, device), a dishwasher, washing machine or dryer in the evening or with the sun (device { start }), an offer price (household offer_eur).

name.description: A short name for the table, e.g. "no battery", "with north side", "with heat pump".

type.description: The edit's type; its fields as in edit_roof (roof_edit_help explains each).

edits.description: edit_roof edits that make this variant from the plan in link, written exactly as for edit_roof (not find_similar, check_outline or search_again).

tools.name: roof_report_pdf
tools.description: The plan behind a solar roof check link as the one-page PDF report the solar roof check page prints, in German, for the person to keep or print: the 3D picture, key figures, the roof from above with its modules, the faces, kWh month by month, self-use with and without battery, the worst shade casters, and a QR code that opens the plan. The PDF comes back inside this answer as an embedded resource (application/pdf, base64); save it as a file. Nothing is stored on the server and no download link is made. This one-shot call waits at most 55 seconds for the page's own report and otherwise answers with a drawn version (same modules; the answer's page_report says why and where the time went); for the page's own report with more time use roof_report_pdf_start. An example, not a quote; the price guide in it is a rough guide, never an offer. With without_price: true the report leaves out the price guide and anything worked out from a price, the QR code and the line to the solar roof check page (which shows the guide) and the sentence promising a visit on site (for an installer's own estimate the report is appended to, so the document carries one price only); that one is always the drawn version. price_shown in the answer says what the file holds: false only when it shows no price of Sky Solar's.

link.description: A solar roof check link (https://pv.skysolar.de/dachcheck/#d=…), as plan_roof, edit_roof or the solar roof check page gave it.

without_price.description: true: the report without Sky Solar's price guide and anything worked out from a price (for appending to an installer's own estimate, so the document carries one price only), and without the QR code and the line that lead to the solar roof check page (which shows the price guide) and without the sentence promising a visit on site; it is then always the drawn version, as the page's own report shows the guide.

tools.name: roof_report_pdf_start
tools.description: The same PDF as roof_report_pdf, made as a background job so a slow render cannot time out your call: this answers at once with a job_id. The page's own report with its 3D picture takes 30 to 150 seconds to draw on the server. Then call roof_report_pdf_status with the job_id every 10 seconds until it says done (or failed, with the reason), and roof_report_pdf_file to get the file. If the page's report cannot be made in time you get the drawn version, and the status says so. without_price: true as for roof_report_pdf (the drawn report without the price guide, done in a few seconds); the job keeps it, so roof_report_pdf_status and roof_report_pdf_file serve that report, and every start gets its own job_id. The finished PDF is kept for 15 minutes under the random job_id; nothing else is stored.

link.description: A solar roof check link (https://pv.skysolar.de/dachcheck/#d=…), as plan_roof, edit_roof or the solar roof check page gave it.

without_price.description: true: the report without Sky Solar's price guide and anything worked out from a price (for appending to an installer's own estimate, so the document carries one price only), and without the QR code and the line that lead to the solar roof check page (which shows the price guide) and without the sentence promising a visit on site; it is then always the drawn version, as the page's own report shows the guide.

tools.name: roof_report_pdf_status
tools.description: Where a roof_report_pdf_start job is: rendering (poll again in 10 seconds), done (summary, which PDF it is and price_shown: whether the file shows a price of Sky Solar's), failed (with a reason code: plan_error, render_error, render_lost) or unknown (wrong or expired job_id). A tool error here means the call itself failed, not the job.

tools.name: roof_report_pdf_file
tools.description: The finished PDF of a roof_report_pdf_start job, inside this answer as an embedded resource (application/pdf, base64); save it as a file, with price_shown as roof_report_pdf gives it. Only when the status says done.

tools.name: roof_picture_start
tools.description: An image (PNG, or JPEG when large) of the plan behind a solar roof check link, drawn by the solar roof check page itself in 3D, from a fixed, named view: front (the start view the page opens with, three-quarters from above), above (straight down, north up), north, east, south or west (from that side, 35° up, about square on to a roof face), or sun (the roof's sun map, "Sonnendach", from above). The same plan and view give the same picture (within a calendar year, while the map data stays the same): the camera follows the house, the sun stands at 21 June, 13:00, nothing moves, no cat and no editing marks, the plan's fine print as on the page. So variants of a plan compare side by side, which screenshots of the page do not (its view moves). Size up to 1600 × 1000 pixels (default). Answers at once with a job_id: the server draws the 3D in software, which takes 30 to 150 seconds. Then call roof_picture_status every 10 seconds until done, and roof_picture_file to get the picture (a JPEG instead of a PNG when the PNG would be over about 1.4 MB). The picture is kept for 15 minutes under the random job_id; nothing else is stored.

link.description: A solar roof check link (https://pv.skysolar.de/dachcheck/#d=…), as plan_roof, edit_roof or the solar roof check page gave it.

view.description: Which view: front (the start view the solar roof check page opens with: three-quarters from above, square on to the main south-facing roof); above (straight down from above, north up); north (from the north, 35° up (about square on to a roof face, and over the neighbours)); east (from the east, 35° up); south (from the south, 35° up); west (from the west, 35° up); sun (the roof's sun ("Sonnendach") on the plain white model, straight down from above, north up: the warmer a spot, the more sun over the year).

tools.name: roof_picture_status
tools.description: Where a roof_picture_start job is: rendering (poll again in 10 seconds), done (with the view, size and plan code), failed (with a reason code: plan_error, render_error, render_lost) or unknown (wrong or expired job_id). A tool error here means the call itself failed, not the job.

tools.name: roof_picture_file
tools.description: The finished picture of a roof_picture_start job, inside this answer as an embedded resource (image/png, or image/jpeg when the PNG was too big; base64) to save as a file; with inline: true as an image content block instead, which most clients show to you, so you can look at it. Only when the status says done.

inline.description: true: the picture as an image content block (image/png or image/jpeg), which most clients show to you, instead of an embedded resource to save as a file.

tools.name: sun_tomorrow
tools.description: What the plan behind a solar roof check link will make tomorrow, from the German Weather Service forecast (Bright Sky): expected kWh and the peak, hour by hour, against what a clear sky would give, sunrise and sunset, and the best stretch of the day to run the dishwasher or charge the car slowly from the roof's own power (with how much of the job the roof covers then). A forecast, cached ten minutes; the plan is read from the link, nothing is stored. Takes the link from plan_roof or edit_roof.

link.description: A solar roof check link (https://pv.skysolar.de/dachcheck/#d=…), as plan_roof, edit_roof or the solar roof check page gave it.

tools.name: consultation_link
tools.description: The form and phone numbers for a free first consultation. The person sends the enquiry themselves; this server cannot book or send anything.

locale.description: Language of the answer: de (German) or en (English).
